obligations.text: By default a package change (load, install, reinstall, update) runs as one IRIS transaction, so a failure rolls back its database writes.
obligations.cases: normal-mode failure (Activate or update step) vs success; transaction on by default
obligations.observation: installed module record/version and journaled step records after the command; $TLEVEL on return
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70 (P load_general/update_steps were not linked from this block; G crate is the coverage-map link)

obligations.text: The rollback includes the dependencies the change loaded for the module.
obligations.cases: parent Activate fails after one or two dependencies loaded (normal mode) vs success
obligations.observation: dependency module records after the command
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70 (G cases B1-C31/C36 agree: dependencies absent after the parent failure)

parent.entailment: The parent states the default rollback itself (graded directly). The children add the scope of a rollback and the two ways to turn it off; no parent obligation is credited by composition.

obligations.text: A database rollback undoes journaled writes in its transaction and does not undo filesystem copies, lock files, CPF effects, pip installs or remote calls.
obligations.cases: failed normal load: journaled record/mapping vs file copy, CPF merge, lock file, pip install, remote call
obligations.observation: which effects remain after the rollback
obligations.gap: failkeep classifies only File, CPF and LocExport as external (an input table). Lock files (OBS-L11), pip installs, remote calls, the archive ModuleRoot replacement (OBS-L7) and the git clone folder have no model: no rule contrasts a lock file or pip install made before an Activate failure with the rolled-back module record.

obligations.text: A failing load that rolled its module record back keeps a FileCopy target copied before the failure, while a deferred copy not yet reached leaves no file; the history Committed bit reflects only the database.
obligations.cases: failure after Activate copy (fail point 3) vs failure at Compile before the deferred copy (fail point 2); history bit
obligations.observation: copied file, module record, history Committed

obligations.text: A direct missing-source copy fails without a copied target file.
A successful copy leaves its file after database rollback.
obligations.basis: alias: resources page owner (#12 there aliases it too)

obligations.text: CPF child exit and applied configuration are separate outputs, read separately from rollback.
A valid role-creation merge survives rollback; an invalid-section merge fails on a disposable provider.

A normal-mode rollback also undoes declared <Mapping> entries and a web application created during the load, while a CPF merge, FileCopy targets and the localization export file written in Activate remain.
obligations.cases: normal load failing after Activate: Mapping, WebApp vs CPF, File, LocExport; success neighbour keeps all
obligations.observation: mapping, web application, CPF configuration, copied file and export file after the command

obligations.text: -DNoTransaction=1 runs the package change without a transaction, so a failure leaves a partial install.
obligations.cases: NoTransaction Activate failure vs default Activate failure (rolled back)
obligations.observation: installed module and resources after the failed command

obligations.text: -DNoJournal=1 turns off process journaling during the change (restored afterwards) and also turns off the transaction.
obligations.cases: NoJournal vs default load: journaling flag during and after the activation; no TSTART
obligations.observation: process journaling flag; $TLEVEL; writes kept after a failure
obligations.basis: reused:coverage-map transaction.opt-out (G crate invariant: journaling off exactly while a NoJournal LoadNewModule holds its JournalManager)

obligations.text: With either flag, a process crash during the change rolls nothing back and may leave the namespace inconsistent.
obligations.cases: kill inside Activate under NoTransaction and under NoJournal vs default (rolled back)
obligations.observation: module state after a process end
obligations.gap: Only NoTransaction kill cases B1-C48T/K are computed (partial kept); l1_alts_kill leaves non-transactional process ends unconstrained (disclosed gap) and no NoJournal crash case is computed. Missing: kill inside Activate under NoJournal showing journaled-off writes kept, against the default kill neighbour.

obligations.text: Both flags apply to install, load, reinstall and update.
obligations.cases: flag given to install/reinstall/update vs load
obligations.observation: transaction use of each command
obligations.gap: update_steps takes `txn` (neither flag) as one input for install/update and never distinguishes NoJournal journaling; reinstall is not modeled. Missing: install and update under each flag with a failing step showing partial writes kept, and the NoJournal journaling-off effect on those paths.

obligations.text: NoTransaction/NoJournal can come from the command line, the namespace default modifiers or the module <Defaults>; a command-line value wins over the other two.

obligations.observation: effective flag value at LoadNewModule
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70 (composition: defmods.merged puts the command line over stored defaults in the shell; loadtx.merge_key puts the command data over the module own <Defaults> at LoadNewModule)

obligations.text: Effective values are merged by key at each LoadNewModule activation; a parent parameter that exists, even zero, overrides the child default.
obligations.cases: parent Some(false) vs child Some(true); parent absent
obligations.observation: effective flag of the child activation

obligations.text: If the parent value is absent, the child own value applies.
obligations.cases: parent None, child Some(true)
obligations.observation: effective flag

obligations.text: A child NoTransaction does not cancel an already-open parent transaction.
obligations.cases: child NoTransaction with parent depth > 0 vs no parent
obligations.observation: transaction depth of the child activation

obligations.text: A child NoJournal disables process journaling during that activation, so its writes can escape the parent rollback.
obligations.cases: child NoJournal write vs journaled child write, parent rolled back
obligations.observation: child writes after the parent rollback
obligations.gap: loadtx takes Write.journal as an input: no rule derives journal=false from the child own <Defaults> NoJournal through effective(). The G crate cannot represent per-module <Defaults> flags (coverage map). Missing: dependency with <Defaults> NoJournal under a failing normal-mode parent, showing its module record kept and the parent rolled back.

obligations.text: Working assumption: a NoJournal dependency keeps its changes when the parent rolls back.
Working assumption: the history record of such a NoJournal dependency must survive the parent rollback and say its changes were kept.
obligations.cases: NoJournal dependency under a failing parent: its History row present with Committed=1 vs absent/0
obligations.observation: dependency History row after the parent rollback
obligations.gap: No model joins dependency <Defaults> NoJournal with History rows. The G crate shows dependency rows lost under the parent rollback (D1) only for journaled dependencies. Missing: the dependency row under journaling off at LoadModuleReference insert time, read by history list/details.

obligations.text: Working assumption (intended): a module that declares NoTransaction must not run inside a transaction opened for its parent, so the change runs without one.
obligations.cases: child NoTransaction inside an open parent transaction
obligations.observation: transaction depth of the child activation
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70 (as built the child stays at the parent depth > 0; the intended promise is contradicted)

obligations.text: Working assumption: require closure consistency (an escaped NoJournal dependency must not remain without its own dependencies); record the observed violating state.
obligations.cases: NoJournal dependency kept after a parent rollback that removed its own dependencies vs consistent closure
obligations.observation: installed modules and their dependency closure
obligations.gap: No model of a NoJournal dependency with its own dependencies (G crate: leaf dependencies only; loadtx: disjoint writes). Missing: dep D (NoJournal) requiring E, parent fails: E rolled back while D stays.
